=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_check_final_merge_ineligibility_alert function, comment_body assignment | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The tracking-issue comment body uses `${alert_hours}` (the configured threshold, default 6) instead of `${elapsed_hours}` (the actual elapsed time).
  WHY: The heading on the preceding line correctly reads "Final merge blocked for ${elapsed_hours}h+" — the body contradicts it by reporting the threshold rather than the real duration; operators reading the comment for situational awareness receive misleading information about how long the merge has genuinely been blocked.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_check_final_merge_ineligibility_alert calls gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/.../pulls/${final_pr}" --jq '.head.sha' to fetch current_sha, then calls _summarize_final_merge_blockers which independently calls gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/.../pulls/${final_pr}" to extract base_ref | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The caller already queries the PR endpoint to get .head.sha; it could extract .base.ref from the same response and pass it to _summarize_final_merge_blockers, avoiding the second round-trip.
  WHY: The waste is one extra GitHub API call per alert firing; the alert path fires rarely, so the operational impact is negligible, but it is a §14 API-hygiene violation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state function (defined, documented, and tested) versus the merge-success path in mark_validation_complete which duplicates the same three-key jq clearing inline alongside status/cycle/counter keys | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The helper exists but is never called from production code, so the inline jq and helper can drift if the key set changes.
  WHY: No current runtime failure — both locations clear the same three keys today — but a future rename or added ineligibility key could leave stale logic in one of the two paths.
- Requirement: "Post-merge verification on PR #2955: confirm the next orchestrator poll cycle merges it." (from PR description test plan, checkbox unchecked)
  Expected change site: No code change expected — this is a live-observation verification step gated on the PR landing on main.
  Evidence of absence: The test plan checkbox is explicitly unchecked in the PR description. The PR diff and LAST RUN DIFF contain no automation, comment marker, or scheduled reminder for this verification step. This is a deferred/manual verification item, not an unimplemented code requirement.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: N/A — deferred requirement; not a gap.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: Operators receive misleading information about stall duration; if a PR has been stuck for 24 hours, the comment still says "at least 6h," understating the actual delay and potentially delaying operator intervention.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:530, 532 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The label "**Blocking check-runs:**" suggests only failing check-runs that would block the merge, but the summary includes all non-acceptable check-runs (pending AND failing) regardless of whether they are in the required set.
  WHY: Operators may misinterpret pending checks as actual blockers.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:462 and 562-564 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Duplicate GitHub API calls to fetch the same PR data. `_check_final_merge_ineligibility_alert` fetches `current_sha` via `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq ... --jq '.head.sha'` at line 462, then `_summarize_final_merge_blockers` fetches the full PR JSON again at lines 562-564 to extract `base_ref`.
  WHY: This adds an extra API round-trip on every alert check; while rare, it violates the API hygiene goal.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:625-631 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state` is defined but never called from production code.
  WHY: The merge-success path at lines 6503-6509 duplicates the same three-key clearing inline instead of calling the helper, creating a maintenance hazard if the key names ever change.
